name: Патові пастки
description:
In the previous lesson, we wanted to avoid a stalemate. We were way up in pieces and wanted to win the game instead of getting a draw.

But when you are losing horribly, a half point is pretty good. A lot better than losing! When the board is nearly empty, stalemates can be a great way to escape losing. You can try to trap the other player into stalemate!

Have a look at example 1. White is way behind, but he does not lose. By sacrificing a queen, he brings about a stalemate. Just watch the moves.

In example 2, White gives up a rook for a stalemate.

Do you plan on sacrificing your last piece to bring about a stalemate? Make sure that the other player is forced to capture. For instance, by using a check.

Now look at example 3. This shows that should not play without thinking. You have two options. One results in stalemate. The other gets you checkmated. 

What do you have to do?
Trap your opponent into stalemate. Sacrifice your last piece to bring about a stalemate. Make sure that your opponent is forced to capture it.

examples.text:
White looks in trouble. He is down two rooks and a pawn. And his king is cramped for space. It won’t be long before White is mated…

But wait! The king has nowhere to move. If it weren’t for the queen, it would be a stalemate.

White can escape losing by handing over his queen!
What a smart trick!
The queen checks the king (green arrow).
The stalemate trap has sprung!
Black must capture to get out of check.
Both players get a half point.

Again, the white king cannot move. White just has to get rid of his rook…

White has to play the right move.

If the rook follows the red arrow, Black’s queen, remote though she is, will take it. Oops, checkmate!

White’s rook should follow the green arrow and give check. Now, Black must use his king to capture. It’s a stalemate!

White can bring about a stalemate by losing his bishop.
He can do two things to sacrifice the bishop.

Only one is good: following the green arrow. Black is in check. He is forced to take the bishop. Stalemate.

Following the red arrow can also result in a stalemate. But only when Black captures the bishop with his rook.
A smarter move for Black is to simply ignore the bishop. He has so many extra pieces that he does not need another one to win the game.
